parsed.why: State-level protection is the strongest documented: public-accommodations law since 2008, all-gender facilities access (2023), hate-crime coverage since 2001, courts ordering care resumed, changeable markers. National border/passport and custody exposure still apply, capping it.

It removed existing gender-identity anti-discrimination protection (first in country), bars local strengthening, bans youth care, and its birth-certificate restroom rule binds all adults on school grounds. Worst legal-risk tier. Only absence of a general adult facility statute keeps it above the harshest.

Harshest tier: facility bans (2024/25), sex defined by birth in statute, birth certificates dual-listing prior marker, court refusing a trans teen's name change, religious-refusal statute, no gender-identity protections. Trans killings at background rate, not a campaign.

Most-protective tier with GENDA public-accommodations coverage, 2024 constitutional amendment, hate-crime law, gender-neutral bathroom mandate, repealed loitering statute, and an operating shield law for visiting care travellers. National border regime still binds at entry.

Real but narrower protection: anti-discrimination in accommodations since 2018, hate-crime enhancements, panic defence abolished, and a 2026 civil-rights judgment for a trans woman. Offset by 2024-26 youth-care bans and a 'least safe' characterisation; raw incident counts lack denominators.
